newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Eletrobras unit to restructure assets.
newsitem.headline: Eletrobras unit to restructure assets.

text.p: Furnas, a power generating unit of Brazil's Eletrobras, said it will restructure assets ahead of its privatization expected at the end of 1997, a Furnas official said.
"This is an important step towards the privatization of the company," said Furnas president Luiz Laercio Simoes Machado.

Under the plan, which will be voted on January 29 at a shareholders meeting, Furnas will transfer its nuclear plants to Eletrobras' subsidiary Nuclen and retain only with its seven hydroelectric and two thermoelectric plants, he said.
Furnas has to transfer its nuclear plants to Nuclen, as nuclear power generation remains a monopoly of the Brazilian government and was not included in the country's privatization program, he said.
According to Machado, the restructuring would improve Furnas' balance sheet by lowering the company's debt levels.

With the transfer of the plants, Furnas' net worth will drop to 9.8 billion reais from a current 13.7 billion and its total debt as a percentage of its net worth will fall to 9 percent from 16 percent, he added.
He said bid specifications to hire consultants to evaluate the firm's assets and draw up a plan to sell off the company would be published by the end of the first quarter.
Eletrobras holds 99.5 percent voting stake in Furnas, which accounts for 38 percent of all energy sold in Brazil.

Furnas has a power generating capacity of 7,500 megawatts. This year and next, the company will inaugurate two new hydroelectric plants in Goias state, increasing its generating capacity by 1,670 megawatts by 1998.
